THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE S VISHWAJITH SHETTY
ORAL ORDER

Accused No.1 in Crime No.321/2024 registered by Jayanagara Police Station, Bengaluru City, for the offences punishable under Sections 376 & 406 r/w 34 of IPC, is before this Court under Section 439 of Cr.P.C, seeking regular bail.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3.

FIR in Crime No.321/2024 was registered by Jayanagara Police Station, Bengaluru city, against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 14.09.2024,
received from Victim girl, aged about 25 years.
During the course of the NC: 2024:KHC:45395 investigation of the case, the petitioner herein was arrested on 15.09.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
4. Bail application filed by the petitioner before the jurisdictional sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.8639/2024 was rejected on 08.10.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case by the victim girl who is co-accused along with the petitioner herein in crime No.267/2024 registered by Jayanagara Police Station, Bengaluru, on the basis of the first information received from Smt.Lalitha Devi, who is the mother of the victim girl.

He submits that Mr Mohammed Arfath Hameed @ Arfath vs State By Sho on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140632260/

Considering the nature of the allegation,
petitioner's custody is no more required.

6. Per contra, learned HCGP and Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the de facto complainant/
the victim girl
have opposed the bail petition.
Learned HCGP submits that allegation found as against the petitioner are serious NC: 2024:KHC:45395 in nature.
Investigation in the case is completed, but charge sheet is not yet filed.
7. Learned Senior Counsel submits that the petitioner is a married man and the victim girl was kept in dark about his marital status.
With an assurance of marrying with the victim girl he had sexual intercourse her.
Consent of the victim girl therefore cannot be considered as consent in the eye of law.
In the event, the petitioner is enlarged on bail he is likely to tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
The petitioner is a person with criminal antecedents.

In support of his arguments, he has placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs State of Maharastra and another, reported in (2019) 9 Supreme Court Cases 608, and prays for dismissal of the petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In the typed first information which was filed by the victim girl, aged about 25 years, on 14.09.2024 before the Jayanagara Police Station, Bengaluru, it is mentioned that she was introduced to the petitioner by her boy friend NC: 2024:KHC:45395 Dashish Dosani in the month of July-2022.
After the petitioner revealed some unpleasant habits of Danish, she had separated from Danish with whom she had a relationship earlier.
Thereafter, she got into a romantic relationship with the petitioner and he introduced her to his family members.
The petitioner allegedly had informed the victim girl that Danish had a private video of her's, and he was demanding money and blackmailing to publish the video online.

Therefore, the victim gave her mother's gold to the petitioner in order to pay money to Danish and his demand kept continuing and she gave her mother's gold as per the demands made by the petitioner and therefore, her mother had given a police complainant before the Jayanagar police station which had resulted in registering FIR in crime No.267/2024 on 31.07.2024.
Only when she was called to the said police station in the said case, after seeing the petitioner in the company of a pregnant woman in the police station, she came to know about his marital status.
She has stated that the petitioner had sexual intercourse with her with a promise to marry her.
Perusal of the material available on record would go to show that the victim girl had relationship with Danish prior to she getting acquainted with the petitioner.
After she discontinued her relationship with Danish, it appears that she had developed relationship the petitioner and they had sexual intercourse.

According to the victim girl the petitioner had informed her that Danish had a private video of her's and he was blackmailing and therefore, the victim girl allegedly had given the gold jewelry of her mother to the petitioner to meets the demands of Danish.

On the basis of the police complaint given by the mother of the victim girl, FIR in crime No.267/2024 was registered by the very same police station and the victim girl is arrayed as accused No.1 in the said FIR.
The petitioner herein is arrayed as accused No.2 in the said case.

sentences.text: 3 10. Material made available before this Court would go to show that the petitioner herein was arrested is crime No.267/2024 on 06.08.2024 and he was enlarged on bail by the trial Court on 12.08.2024.

According to the victim NC: 2024:KHC:45395 girl, after FIR in crime No.267/2024 was registered on 31.07.2024, when she had gone to the police station she had found the petitioner herein in the company of a pregnant woman in the police station.

FIR in the present case has been filed on 14.09.2024 much after the petitioner was released on bail in Crime No.267/2024.
11.
Learned HCGP has submitted before this Court that investigation in the case is already completed.

Except the aforesaid case the only other case registered against the petitioner is in Crime No.782/2024 by Banasawadi Police Station Bengaluru, for the offences punishable under Section 103 of Karnataka Police Act, 1963, Sections 21, 24 & 20(2) of Cigarettes and others Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production,
Supply and Distribution) Rules- 2004 and Section 77 of Juvenile Justice Act, 2000.

entities.text:
Cigarettes and others Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production,
Supply and Distribution) Rules- 2004
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Allegation as against the petitioner in the said case is that he along with other accused persons had opened a Hookabar within the jurisdiction of Banasawadi Police station, Bengaluru.
It is not in dispute that in the other NC: 2024:KHC:45395 two cases the petitioner is on bail.

Insofar as the present case is concerned, considering the nature of allegations found against the petitioner in the present case and also having regard to the fact that investigation in the case is already completed, I am of opinion that the petitioner's prayer for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.

12. Judgment in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs State of Maharastra and another, has been rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case where petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C filed by the accused was dismissed by the High Court.

entities.text: Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs State of Maharastra and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court having set aside the orders passed by the High Court of Bombay, has quashed the entire proceedings as against the accused in the said case.
The question whether consent was based on misconception of fact is a matter to be proved before the trial Court and at this stage, no finding can be recorded about the same.
Therefore, I am of the view that judgment in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs State of Maharastra and NC: 2024:KHC:45395 another, cannot be made applicable to the present case.

entities.text: Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs State of Maharastra and NC: 2024:KHC:45395 another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.
